text: First principles is a kind of physics way of looking at the world. And what that really means is you boil things down to the most fundamental truths and then reason up from there.
sourceName: Startup Archive — Elon Musk explains first principles thinking (Kevin Rose interview, 2012)

text: So first principles thinking would be to say, okay, what are the material constituents of the batteries? What is the spot market value of the material constituents? It's got cobalt, nickel, aluminum, carbon, some polymers for separation, and a steel can. So break that down on a material basis and say, okay, if we bought that on the London Metal Exchange, what would each of those things cost? It's $80/kWh. So clearly, you just need to think of clever ways to take those materials and combine them into the shape of a battery cell. And then you can have batteries that are much, much cheaper than anyone realizes.
sourceName: Startup Archive — Elon Musk on first principles and battery costs (Kevin Rose interview, 2012)

text: A company has no value in itself. It only has value to the degree that is an effective allocator of resources to create business services that are of a greater value than the costs of the inputs.
sourceName: CNBC — Elon Musk on the problem with corporate America: 'Too many MBAs' (WSJ CEO Council, Dec 2020)

text: I think that there might be too many MBAs running companies.
sourceName: CNBC — Elon Musk on the problem with corporate America: 'Too many MBAs' (WSJ CEO Council, Dec 2020)

text: There should be more focus on the product or service itself, less time on board meetings, less time on financials.
sourceName: CNBC — Elon Musk on the problem with corporate America: 'Too many MBAs' (WSJ CEO Council, Dec 2020)

text: When I have spent too much time in a conference room, that's when things have gone awry, and when I go spend time on the factory floor or really using the cars, thinking about the rockets, that's where things have gone better.
sourceName: CNBC — Elon Musk on the problem with corporate America: 'Too many MBAs' (WSJ CEO Council, Dec 2020)

text: When something is important enough, you do it even if the odds are not in your favor.
sourceName: Snopes (verified) — Elon Musk on SpaceX's odds (CBS 60 Minutes, 2012)

text: The speed of the production ramp is inversely proportionate to how many new parts and steps there are.
sourceName: Elon Musk on X — on production ramps (via AOL)
